articles.title: Lamine Yamal stars again as Spain see off Czechia and maintain perfect start
articles.summary: Lamine Yamal says he feels like Superman or Spider-Man sometimes, and Spain’s fans are starting to wonder if he just might be. There is something comic book hero about what the teenager is doing right now, some unexplained super power swelling inside him.
body: And yet in a game which seemed to have been done at half-time, when Spain led 2-0 after Rodrigo Hernandez had added the second and Lamine Yamal was withdrawn, his show seemingly over, the danger returned. Czechia, vastly improved after the break, pulled one back through Jiri Slama on 69 and then were denied a 79th-minute equaliser when Vassilis Fotias, the referee, who rescued Spain, harshly ruled out a Ryan Naderi goal – apparently for a foul on Robin Le Normand as the free-kick that led to it was swung in.

Reduced to ten men soon after, still furious, Czechia finally fell with two minutes left when Mikel Merino made Spain safe. The seleccion’s first visit to the Carlos Tartiere in eleven years had ended the way they had hoped. Welcomed back as World and European champions once more, they were applauded off as winners again. A night that had begun with Rodri being presented with the World Cup by Santi Cazorla and Juan Mata, academy products at Real Oviedo and members of the generation to which all others would forever be compared, ended with a jeopardy no one anticipated when it started in a way that has become implausibly, absurdly familiar.

Scotland remain alive and kicking in section B1 of the Nations League while aware they will face far, far stiffer challenges. Scotland needed to be professional in North Macedonia and met that task appropriately.

McGinn’s response was as forceful as his teammate.

articles.title: Celtic condemn fan protest as Desmond targeted at Alfred Dunhill
articles.summary: Celtic's largest shareholder Dermot Desmond is targeted in a protest at the Alfred Dunhill Links golf tournament in St Andrews as tennis balls were thrown towards him.
body: Celtic say they will "indefinitely ban" anyone "established to be involved in planning, facilitating or participating" in a protest against the club's largest shareholder Dermot Desmond at the Alfred Dunhill Links golf tournament in St Andrews.

Tennis balls with pictures of the 76-year-old's face scored out were thrown on to the green of the 15th hole of the pro-am competition, with images showing Desmond later having to be escorted off the course by security.
The statement from the club "condemns in the strongest terms" the incident, which is said was "discussed and planned in advance".

"This was a premeditated action," it added. "Accordingly, the club will no longer recognise the Celtic Fans Collective as a representative body speaking on behalf of Celtic supporters and will cease all engagement with the Collective."

articles.title: Where will Thomas Castellanos be for Texas Tech football game at Colorado?
articles.summary: BOULDER, Colo. — Backup quarterback Thomas Castellanos, prevented by a court order from playing in the Texas Tech football game against Colorado on Saturday, Oct. 3, will be with the team in street clothes at Folsom Field, an athletics department spokesman said.
body: Castellanos played in the first four games based on a court ruling that enabled class of 2022 college freshmen to receive a fifth year, putting those players at odds with the NCAA's new age-based eligibility model, commonly referred to as 5 for 5. Under the NCAA's new model, Castellanos' eligibility expired at the end of last season when he had played four years without redshirting.
A court ruling Friday in Kentucky dissolved a temporary restraining order through which Castellanos and other players party to the suit had been allowed to play.

The Red Raiders learned of the newest court order in Kentucky that changed Castellanos' 2026 status while the team was en route to Colorado the day before the game. A Tech spokesman confirmed Friday that Castellanos will not play in the Colorado game.

The Red Raiders appear relatively healthy for the game. Starting tight end Terrance Carter Jr. was on the field in team workout attire during early pre-game warmup. Carter was listed as probable during the Big 12-mandated Friday availability update.

articles.title: 'It means everything' - numbers behind Robertson's 100-cap Scotland career
articles.summary: Andy Robertson has become only the second man ever to play 100 times for Scotland. BBC Sport Scotland charts his international career in numbers.
body: Andy Robertson says reaching 100 Scotland caps "means everything to me" after he hit the milestone in Saturday's Nations League win in North Macedonia.
Goals by Kieron Bowie and John McGinn ensured the Scots recorded their first win under new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli and gave the captain a victory to make his flagship appearance.
"It means everything to me, it means everything to my family," Tottenham Hotspur's Robertson told BBC Sport Scotland. "I've been away now 100 times... I've got to feel sorry for my wife!

"It's been an unbelievable journey, I remember my first game and it's been a process since then. It's emotional for me. I love this country, there's only one person before me in the men's game to do that, it's a pretty special achievement."

articles.title: Vikings Elevate Johnny Hekker from Practice Squad
articles.summary: Ahead of Sunday’s game at U.S. Bank Stadium against the Miami Dolphins, the Minnesota Vikings have just one practice squad elevation for this week, but with the way things have gone in the first three weeks, it could be a very important one.
body: The Vikings have elevated punter Johnny Hekker from the practice squad, meaning that he will handle punting and holding duties for the second week in a row as Brett Thorson continues to deal with a hamstring injury. It’s important to note that this is Hekker’s first elevation from the practice squad this year. Ahead of last week’s game against Tampa Bay, Hekker was signed from the practice squad to the 53-man roster, not elevated, so he still has two more elevations remaining after this one and will not have to be released after the game as he was last week.

In last week’s game, Hekker was called upon eight times and performed well, averaging 46.5 yards with a long of 63 and placing two punts inside the 20-yard line. He also, as far as I could tell, did a solid job of holding on all three of Will Reichard’s field goal attempts and both extra points. If he hadn’t...well, we’d obviously know.

articles.summary: Sebastien Pocognoli secured his first Scotland win at the third time of asking as captain Andy Robertson became just the second player to reach 100 caps.
body: The head coach insisted there was no extra pressure after drawing a blank in their opening two Nations League games, but he and the players silenced some critics with a strong performance in Skopje despite a second red card inside a week as they beat North Macedonia 2-0.

Robertson missed two brilliant chances before Kieron Bowie - hooked after Jack Hendry's early sending off against Switzerland in midweek - smashed the ball into the bottom corner to earn his first international goal and Scotland's first in over 420 minutes.
Play was stopped by a dog running onto the pitch before Scotland continued to dominate with Bowie, Robertson and Ben Gannon-Doak going close before the break.
Scotland were awarded a penalty when Gannon-Doak went down in the box after half-time, only for the referee to overturn his decision after being called to the monitor.

articles.title: 'Our boys can't believe it' - Powell on Wakefield's 'phenomenal, immense' title run
articles.summary: Wakefield Trinity head coach Daryl Powell revealed members of his playing squad were in shock following their stunning Super League Grand Final victory, two years on from playing in England's second tier.
body: Wakefield were crowned Super League champions for the first time in the club's history with a resounding 23-10 victory over Warrington Wolves in the Grand Final at Old Trafford, a week on from travelling to huge favourites Wigan Warriors and dispatching of them 33-6 in the semi-finals.

The success proved Wakefield's first league title for 58 years dating back to 1968, and all the more remarkable considering they were relegated from Super League in 2023, playing the 2024 season in the Championship under Powell.
"I'm just amazed really at the players and how good they've been," Powell said.
"Obviously it's pretty sweet for me as an individual but for the club, the players, the coaching staff, everything that we've built up over the last three years is phenomenal.

body: It is the first time Wakefield have made the Grand Final and they achieved their greatest glory on their first attempt.
They also become the sixth winner of Super League, joining Wigan Warriors, St Helens, Leeds Rhinos, Bradford Bulls and Hull KR.
It rounds out a fairy-tale story for Wakefield who were relegated in 2023, returned to Super League in the 2025 season, and have now written themselves into the history books as champions.
Wakefield held a dominant 19-0 half-time lead thanks to converted tries from Cameron Scott, Isaiah Vagana and Jazz Tevaga, Max Jowitt staying calm under pressure with the boot.
